flagged: F001: The section establishes the shared z=.438 external and internal shoulder, followed by the separately toleranced .4380 internal land. For the printed 15-degree cone, 0.267949192431123 is tan(15 degrees), and 1.303225372841206 is sec(15 degrees)+tan(15 degrees). The inspection balls touch the end-face inspection plane: their centers are .500/2 behind that face. Thus end-seat radius=(inspection gap+ball diameter)/2 + ball diameter/2*(sec15+tan15). The 45-degree outer shoulder has equal axial and radial increments.

F008: The .500 dimension in the longitudinal section locates the bottom of the local end-face relief, not an axisymmetric counterbore. The cap center lies on the vertical centerline at 1.812. Preserve the printed .188 radius independently of the .377 overall width.

F009: The relief opens into the central bore as shown in Detail C and the section. Extend the rectangle to the axis, already inside the bore, rather than terminating tangentially on the cone. Combining the printed width .377, left offset .188, and cap radius .188 leaves a .001 nominal ledge on the right at the cap spring line; preserve these independent dimensions for review rather than silently substituting a .1885 radius or centered width.

F010: The section shows the drilling beginning at the relief floor. Model .69 depth to full diameter with a flat bottom under standard blind-hole drafting convention. Preserve the anomalous printed thread class rather than silently changing it.
F011: Section B-B establishes through flange holes. Use the overall length as drilling depth to overshoot the flange, and retain the printed Cartesian positions.
F012: The end view shows mirror-image horizontal-axis holes.
F013: The section establishes through flange holes; overall-length drilling overshoots the flange. End-view symmetry establishes the negative-coordinate seed.
F014: The end view shows symmetry about both centerlines. A Cartesian grid preserves the printed basic coordinates.
F015: The section shows the counterbore on the z=1.75 face and the smaller drill breaking into the large-end recess. Overall-length drilling overshoots all material on this line.
F016: Top and bottom holes are symmetric about the horizontal centerline.

F017: The section establishes counterbore side and through drill; overall-length drilling overshoots all material. End-view symmetry supplies negative seed coordinates. Do not substitute an exact hexagon.
F018: The oblique holes mirror across both centerlines; retain their coordinates independently of the 2.438 vertical radius.
F019: Section B-B shows the small passage through the hub wall between the hub shoulder and large-end recess.
F020: At radius 2.406 the large-end face is recessed to z=.438 by the 5.508 bore. Section B-B confirms this is the entry surface for the reverse-side steps.
F021: Both reverse-side depths originate at the same recessed large-end face at z=.438.
F022: The lower longitudinal section shows the axial passage communicating with the radial drilling and large-end recess; use a through hole rather than a coincident termination.

F023: Auxiliary A and the lower section show one radial drilling from the 5.750 outside diameter into the 2.7515 bore at axial station 1.250. The .469 callout is preparation followed by the .5003 finished bore; no retained smaller step is depicted. Entry is 30 degrees toward -X from downward vertical, or 240 degrees from +X. Add one finished-hole diameter to the radial wall thickness to clear the curved inner surface without reaching the opposite wall.
